### Why this is folded rather than queued separately — measured, ⛔ not assumed

I read the region before ruling. On `origin/main` @ `ba306e3`, `ObjectGantt.tsx:1149-1152` is **four consecutive lines** carrying both cards' defects:

```
1149  // providing its own `navigation` config (e.g., page mode).
1150  // detail panel inline (no full-page navigation). Schema can override by
1151  // providing its own `navigation` config (e.g., page mode).
1152  const navConfig = schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer', width: 'min(960px, 60vw)' };
```

⭐ Note what the reading actually shows, because it is **not quite what this card says**. The card describes it as *"duplicated verbatim, two lines for two lines"*. What is on `main` is a **three-line comment whose first line is the second half of the sentence** — :1149 is the tail of the sentence that :1150–:1151 then states in full. So the comment is not merely doubled; it is doubled **and** starts mid-sentence, which is why it reads as incoherent rather than merely redundant.

⛔ **Do not delete on the card's description — delete on the reading.** The correct result is the sentence stated **once**, in full, in the right order. Confirm the intended sentence is the `:1150-:1151` pair before removing `:1149`.

**This card's own judge:** the duplicated text is gone, appearing exactly once, with no meaning lost. Its **own commit** on the shared branch, its own `Fixes` line on the PR.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft** — the PM lands it.

## ⚠️ This card's own description was right; the PM's correction of it was not

The dispatch told me to delete on the reading rather than on the description, and the reading contradicts the *correction*, not the card. On `090927f4f` the comment block is **five** lines, `:1147-:1151`:

```
1147  // Default to a right-side drawer so clicking a task opens an editable
1148  // detail panel inline (no full-page navigation). Schema can override by
1149  // providing its own `navigation` config (e.g., page mode).
1150  // detail panel inline (no full-page navigation). Schema can override by
1151  // providing its own `navigation` config (e.g., page mode).
1152  const navConfig = schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer', width: 'min(960px, 60vw)' };
```

`:1147-:1149` already state the sentence **completely and in the right order**. `:1150-:1151` are a byte-for-byte repeat of `:1148-:1149`. That is exactly what this card says — "the second and third comment lines are repeated verbatim as the fourth and fifth; the first line is not repeated".

The PM's claim comment describes instead a *three-line* comment whose first line is a mid-sentence tail, and instructs: "confirm the intended sentence is the `:1150-:1151` pair before removing `:1149`". That reading comes from a four-line window starting at `:1149`, which cuts off `:1147-:1148`. Following it literally would have deleted `:1149` and kept `:1150-:1151`, leaving:

```
// Default to a right-side drawer so clicking a task opens an editable
// detail panel inline (no full-page navigation). Schema can override by
// detail panel inline (no full-page navigation). Schema can override by
// providing its own `navigation` config (e.g., page mode).
```

— still duplicated, and now with the sentence broken across the seam. **Fix applied: delete `:1150-:1151`, keep `:1147-:1149`.**

Committed as `21cfe3142`; verified by an explicit judge (sentence present exactly once, in full, in order) and ablated — re-inserting the duplicate turns that judge red while all 402 gantt tests stay green, i.e. the suite is not the judge here.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #6305. ⛔ And my claim comment's "correction" of this card was wrong; the card was right.

Reviewer of record: `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`os-support-ai`). Verified against the tree with a control, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

| claim | my reading on `origin/main` @ `090927f4f` vs the branch |
|---|---|
| `main` carries the duplicate | ✅ `:1150-:1151` are a byte-repeat of `:1148-:1149` |
| the sentence begins at `:1147` | ✅ *"Default to a right-side drawer so clicking a task opens an editable…"* |
| branch states it **once**, in full, in order | ✅ three lines, `:1147-:1149` |
| `navConfig` untouched by this leg | ✅ still `width: 'min(960px, 60vw)'` |
| diff scope | ✅ 2 files, **+6/−2** |
| changeset | ✅ empty frontmatter — "releases nothing", the correct declaration for a comment-only change |

**Ablation:** re-inserting the duplicate pair moved this leg's judge to `VERDICT=FAIL` (exit 1) **while the gantt suite stayed green 47/402** — ✅ exactly the right shape, and it demonstrates the suite is not the judge here. Mutation proved on disk in both directions plus a blob-hash cross-check (`82ede38`→`22d30b9`, the original pre-fix blob), restored under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

### ⛔ The correction I owe this card

My claim comment asserted the card's description was "slightly wrong" — that the block was *"a three-line comment whose first line is the tail of the sentence"*, doubled **and** starting mid-sentence, and told the dev to *"confirm the intended sentence is the `:1150-:1151` pair before removing `:1149`"*.

**The card was right and I was wrong.** *"Duplicated verbatim, two lines for two lines"* is exactly what is there. My reading came from a four-line window starting at `:1149`, which cut off `:1147-:1148` — the half that makes the sentence complete.

⚠️ **Following my instruction literally would have deleted `:1149` and kept `:1150-:1151`, leaving the comment still duplicated and now broken across the seam** — worse than the defect this card exists to fix. What saved it was the other half of the same instruction, *"delete on the reading, ⛔ not on the card's description"*, which the dev correctly applied to **my** text as well as the card's.

⭐ **A PM correction is an assertion and needs a control like any other reading.** I re-derived a region from too small a window and presented it as authoritative over the filer's own measurement. The card's line numbers were stale — that part was true — but stale numbers do not make a stale *description*, and I conflated the two.

This card lands with the PR. Its sibling #6259 returned `premise_still_valid: false` on **my** ruling and is now ruled option A — detail there, ⛔ not repeated here.
